title: CMT Swap Valuation and OAS on a Rate Tree

maps.tested: The sheet reduces the whole chapter to one item: 'CMT swap'. A recall confirms it appeared with an OAS wrapper.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'decision tree question with OAS of CMT swap'. LO 12.h is the exact objective: value a constant-maturity Treasury swap given an interest-rate tree and risk-neutral probabilities. LO 12.d, the true-vs-risk-neutral probability distinction applied to interest-rate drift, is the conceptual partner and a standing polarity trap.

vardeezReading: MR-12: Moderate, with the note "a) CMT swap".

selectors.name: CMT swap value on a two-period tree
selectors.what: Value a constant-maturity Treasury swap paying N x (yCMT - K)/2 every six months, working backward through a two-period rate tree with risk-neutral probabilities: each date-1 node = [p x Vup + (1 - p) x Vdown]/(1 + r_node/2) + that node's own payment, then discount to date 0 with the date-0 probability; the question may wrap this in an OAS.
selectors.theory: Why the swap is valued by expected discounted value under risk-neutral probabilities, why each node value includes its own payment as well as the discounted next-date expectation, and why the probability at date 1 (q) is solved separately from the one at date 0 (p).

selectors.name: OAS: shift discounting only, cheap or rich
selectors.what: Option-adjusted spread: the spread added to the tree's discount rates (never to the rates that set the cash flows) so that the model value equals the market price; positive OAS means market price below model value (cheap), negative OAS means rich.
selectors.theory: Why the OAS enters discounting only, why the sign gives cheap versus rich, and that under the risk-neutral process the expected return of a security is the short rate plus the OAS per period.

selectors.name: True versus risk-neutral probabilities and drift
selectors.what: Explain the difference between true and risk-neutral probabilities and compute the drift they imply over a step of plus or minus delta: drift = p x delta - (1 - p) x delta = (2p - 1) x delta, with the real-world probabilities (often 0.5) supplied as the tempting wrong input; only risk-neutral probabilities recover market prices.
selectors.theory: Risk-neutral probabilities put more weight on the high-rate (low-price) states, so the risk-neutral drift is positive when the true drift is zero; the risk-neutral and not the true probabilities determine the arbitrage price.

notSelected: MR-12 a (expected discounted value is not price), b (replication of a call on a zero), c (risk-neutral pricing of options), e (multi-period extension), g (recombining trees), i (size of the time step) and j (BSM for bonds) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer; MR-12 d, f and h are covered only through S1 to S3.
